sourceChecks.claim: Live AWS comparison explains logical block addresses and specific-block updates, plus filesystem names/directories over block storage; linked EBS setup confirms attach is distinct from filesystem creation. Database transaction responsibilities checked against PostgreSQL transaction documentation.

Live EBS setup instructs identifying devices, checking existing filesystems, skipping mkfs for existing data including snapshot restores, and mounting at a directory-tree location. This supports every setup distinction and the destructive-format warning.

Live EBS Features Data availability and Data persistence sections specify same-AZ attachment/replication and configurable DeleteOnTermination. No cross-zone live access or undeletability follows from this; lesson correctly scopes the claims.

Live fsync DESCRIPTION/RETURN VALUE/ERRORS specify file cache and metadata flushing, waiting for device completion, directory-fsync distinction and failure returns. Follow-up fflush documents application-buffer versus kernel-buffer scope; neither promises multi-write transactions or survival of arbitrary disasters.

Live EBS Multi-Attach considerations explicitly reject simultaneous XFS/EXT4 access, require clustered software and application write ordering, and limit eligible attachments. This supports the cache/metadata conflict explanation and coordination boundary.

Live EBS Create snapshots specifies point-in-time written-volume state, exclusion of application/OS caches, asynchronous pending state and write-pause preparation. EBS setup supports unformatted restore mounting. PostgreSQL file-backup documentation distinguishes consistent snapshots and recovery requirements. Retention and restore testing are justified operational checks, not snapshot guarantees.

Live EBS I/O characteristics defines IOPS, end-to-end latency and pending queue length; its small/large I/O examples show operation versus byte limits. It explicitly identifies EC2 bandwidth and insufficient demand as limiting factors. Lesson avoids universal performance promises.

Live EBS volumes describes attached hard-drive-like storage for system drives/database updates. AWS comparison supports named shared files versus addressed blocks and object identifiers; PostgreSQL transactions supports the separate database role. Earlier setup/recovery sources substantiate remaining operator responsibilities.
